highlights.title: Russian man linked to deadly London hospitals hack arrested
highlights.summary: The 28-year-old detained by German police is accused of being part of the cyber-crime gang that hacked blood-test firm Synnovis in 2024.
body: German police have detained a Russian man accused of being part of a cyber-crime gang which caused chaos at London hospitals and contributed to a patient's death.
The hack of blood testing company Synnovis in 2024 led to disrupted pathology services across several London hospitals and was the first cyber attack in history to be directly linked to a death.
The BBC can confirm German detectives are now including the incident in their investigation into the detained Russian and his associates.
Separately, the BBC has learned that British police are examining whether its own inquiry may lead to an unlawful killing case - potentially a world first in cyber-crime.

highlights.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’
highlights.summary: MIT professor Sherry Turkle warns that people have become dangerously enmeshed with chatbots.
body: During four decades of studying the effects of interaction with computers, Sherry Turkle has developed a reputation as a careful if critical social scientist who approaches her work with academic rigor and distance.

Her new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, breaks this mold. It is a polemic warning that we have reached a state of emergency where our humanity is at risk from overreliance on soulless machines who pose as our tutors, mentors, friends, colleagues, and lovers. Turkle is aiming for the high bar of books — Silent Spring, The Jungle, Unsafe at Any Speed —that awaken the public to impending crises.
Essentially, this diminutive MIT professor is taking on a multitrillion-dollar industry backed by a government eager to accelerate AI into every corner of our personal and professional lives.

STEVEN LEVY: Your previous books reported results of your research as a social scientist, often leading to troubling conclusions about how people, especially children, interact with computers. But this book reads like you’re breaking the glass and pulling the fire alarm. Why the shift?

highlights.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
highlights.summary: One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.
body: But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.
The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.

highlights.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Is Getting Huge Changes Next Week
highlights.summary: At the end of September, The Blood of Dawnwalker director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz revealed to Eurogamer that a big patch was in store for the vampire RPG. That massive update is finally on its way.
body: The developer revealed the highlights of the upcoming patch in a post on the game's official X account. It will introduce an even easier version of the game's current Story mode, while the existing Story mode will now be called Forgiving. The patch also adds Draught of Mind Rebirth, which essentially lets players reset all their unlocked abilities. The game will also get directional animal petting so you can finally make friends with all the dogs and cats in Vale Sangora.

The most glaring omission in the patch 1.1 feature list is New Game Plus, something fans have been asking for since the game's launch. Tomaszkiewicz has said the team is looking into the feature, but that he can't say anything yet. Rebel Wolves hasn't said exactly when the new patch will be released, or if it will come to all platforms at the same time.

Rebel Wolves is touting that patch 1.1 will include over 1,000 improvements and fixes. That is sure to make the overall experience much smoother for players. Here's what we know is coming in The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.1.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

highlights.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: ‘Safe Exit’ Director Mohammed Hammad on Staying True to His Vision: ‘I Need to Be Free as a Filmmaker’
highlights.summary: Mohammed Hammad’s “Safe Exit” received an Atlas Prize for Post-production at the 2025 Atlas Workshops of the Marrakech Film Festival before making its debut in the Panorama section of the 2026 Berlinale.
body: How have you negotiated the difficulties of getting an independent film made in Egypt now? “Safe Exit” is completely self-funded. We formed a new production company, Pariedolia Productions, and now we’re trying to distribute the film through that company, which is a challenge. We’ve chosen this model because many studios in Egypt tend to avoid this kind of film, especially given the topics it covers. Even getting the necessary permissions to shoot the film was very hard. But together with my producer Kholoud Saad I knew I needed to make this film, just like we made “Withered Green.”

What about your co-producers? The main co-producer is Dora Bouchoucha with Nomadis Images, from Tunisia. And Ibrahim El-Battout, one of the godfathers of independent cinema in Egypt, is also a co-producer. Ibrahim was with me from the beginning, also as an adviser, and I trust him completely. We worked on pre-production together, in conjunction with Kholoud; Ibrahim is one of Egypt’s leading independent filmmakers, along with Khairy Beshara and Yousry Nasrallah, and he was with us throughout the shooting, every day.

highlights.title: I travel 200,000 miles a year. These are the five carry-on suitcases I actually trust
highlights.summary: In an endless sea of suitcase options, these are the best to save you time and money. The best travel backpack. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: There are few worse feelings than climbing off an all-day flight, shambling on down to baggage claim, and then watching each and every one of your fellow passengers gleefully grab their bag and disappear, while yours is nowhere to be found. The devastating realization that your checked suitcase didn’t make it is a strong enough blow to turn the sweetest of vacations sour.

I’ve been there, and that’s just one of the many reasons I never check a bag unless I absolutely have to. But living the carry-on life requires having the right suitcase, and there are hundreds and hundreds of choices out there. We tested 15 models and considered dozens more to find the perfect one for you.

I make my living as a freelance journalist, but finding the story often means hopping on a plane and jetting somewhere far away. I fly about 200,000 miles every year, endure 150 days away from home, and set down in a dozen countries or more.

highlights.title: Elon Musk Is Almost Single-Handedly Funding the Republican Midterms Push
highlights.summary: Elon Musk has assembled a presidential-level field operation this midterm cycle, underscoring the extent to which he has taken over the get-out-the-vote effort for the Republican party.
body: Elon Musk has quietly financed a major canvassing operation to help Republican candidates in the midterm elections that rivals his effort in the 2024 presidential election, according to federal filings posted Thursday night. To monitor the trillionaire’s overall influence on November’s elections, WIRED created a l ive-updating tracker that pulls federal filings daily.

The Musk-aligned America PAC has spent $76.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, $35.8 million of which has been spent on a field operation to drive turnout among President Donald Trump's core base across all seven Senate battleground states and a number of House races, the filings show.

That compares with the roughly $45 million America PAC had spent on putting together a field operation at the same point in the 2024 cycle, when the super PAC effectively ran the vast majority of canvassing for Trump's presidential campaign.

highlights.title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
highlights.summary: Meta's new terms appear to give it permission to crawl and scrape websites "associated" with the businesses that use its platforms - including online publishers, according to a report from Nieman Lab.
body: The new policy allows Meta to crawl all websites ‘associated’ with a business account.

While Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says that the company is just “consolidating” its commercial and self-serve ad terms, legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” like a site’s robots.txt file. That could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.

Roberts pushes back on Nieman Lab ’s reporting, saying “There is no change to how Meta uses web crawlers; any suggestion to the contrary is false… Content owners can still use robots.txt flags to indicate their preferences, as we clearly explain in our developer documentation.” Meta has followed OpenAI in striking AI licensing deals with CNN, Fox News, USA Today, and People Inc., but these terms could give the company access to a much broader swath of content.

highlights.title: 'I'm telling you the truth' - Carrick insists Martinez situation resolved
highlights.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick insists he is telling the truth when he says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's post-match outburst earlier this week.
body: In a press conference dominated by questions about Martinez, Carrick revealed that the defender would be included in Sunday's squad for the trip to Leeds United despite him calling out director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of investment in the transfer window.

Martinez, whose outspoken comments came after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox. CEO Omar Berrada and Carrick, on Thursday before making an apology over the timing and public nature of his criticism.
Asked about Martinez on Friday ahead of Sunday's trip to Leeds, live on Sky Sports, Carrick said: "He's released his statement and realised he made a mistake.
"That's enough for us to move on with. From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done is enough to move on."

body: Developer Infinity Ward issued a statement, asking people to please not spoil the story. "We've one one ask. Let everyone experience it for themselves. Keep the campaign spoilers under wraps," Infinity Ward said. "Time to go dark."

MW4 is expected to wrap up the current Modern Warfare storyline that began with 2019's Modern Warfare. Activision boss Tyler Bahl told The Game Business that MW4 is the "epic conclusion of the recent series of Modern Warfare."

"It’s not that some characters and pieces can’t live on beyond this and be reinvented. But we’re excited by closing this chapter and launching a new one," he said. "Where we go with future games, we have to innovate."
To that end, Bahl also confirmed that a new sub-franchise for Call of Duty is in the works after years of Modern Warfare and Black Ops games.

highlights.title: Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Makes $4 Million in Previews, ‘You Can See Everything’ Behind With $1.75 Million
highlights.summary: Several new challengers are stepping into the box office ring this weekend to face off. Paramount’s “Street Fighter” video game adaptation should lead the pack of newcomers. It made $4 million in Thursday previews at the box office, and it’s expected to make $25 million to $35 million in its debut.
body: The highly anticipated Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything ” from A24 made $1.75 million in previews and is aiming for third place with $7 million to $8 million, a stellar debut for a non-fiction doc. The movie cost just $7 million to produce and has been building hype since it had a surprise debut at last month’s Telluride Film Festival. Directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim secretly filmed Elizabeth Holmes ahead of her 11-year prison sentence and even lived with the disgraced Theranos founder to get full access to her life. It’s expected to be a rare box office hit for a documentary and could even land in this year’s Oscar race.

The final newcomer this weekend is Focus Features’ Jane Austen adaptation of “ Sense and Sensibility,” which cost $25 million and is on track to make $5 million to $8 million this weekend. It made $1.15 million from advance screenings and previews. The new take on the classic novel stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, who navigate love, loss and financial uncertainty as they are forced to leave their family estate in Sussex.

highlights.title: Judith Lucy on her cancer diagnosis: ‘I’m a bit over getting so much material out of my life’
highlights.summary: One of Australia’s hardest-working comedians is still laughing at the timing of a breast cancer diagnosis just as she set out to launch a book about wellness. Two days out from surgery, she talks burnout, Buddhism and saying goodbye to her boobs. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: Judith Lucy cannot get a cold. A few hours before I’m due to meet her for a walk around the rose gardens and classic conservatory of the St Kilda Botanical Gardens, a stone’s throw from her home in Melbourne’s south-east, the beloved comedian is on a telehealth call from the front seat of her publicist’s car.

Her doctor needs to go over the results from the previous day’s scans to confirm everything is looking good – good enough to perform the double mastectomy they have planned for Friday, three weeks after she was diagnosed with breast cancer. The cancer isn’t appearing anywhere else on the scans, she learns, but a compromised immune system going into surgery would throw the whole thing out of whack. So with the blustery wind and grey skies at our backs, we retreat into her home instead. The walk up and down the hallway, from the front door of her lovely weatherboard cottage to the neat living room at the back will have to make do for our very short walk.

highlights.title: Analogue is re-releasing its SNES and Genesis consoles with some nice upgrades
highlights.summary: Analogue announced new versions of its Super Nt and Mega Sg retro consoles today with a "reworked industrial design" and built-in wireless connectivity for controllers and accessories.
body: The Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus add USB-C and USB-A ports plus built-in wireless connections for controllers.

Although neither of the new consoles allows SNES or Genesis titles to be played in 4K like the Analogue 3D does with Nintendo 64 titles, the 1080p Super Nt and Mega Sg Plus add a USB-C port so you can power them with the cables you already use with your phone and mobile devices, and an additional USB-A port for other peripherals. Both consoles also introduce a built-in Bluetooth or a low-latency 2.4Ghz wireless connection for connecting to gamepads without requiring an additional controller port dongle.

Wired controllers are still an option, and the upgraded consoles can both be powered up remotely using whatever gamepad is connected as the primary controller. Analogue also says game cartridges can now be hot swapped without having to completely power down either console after quitting the game through a menu.
Both the Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus will be available for preorder starting on October 19th at 9AM PT/11AM ET for $219.99 with shipping expected to start sometime in December, later this year.

highlights.title: AI-Generated Hot Girls Are Ripping Off Comedians to Boost Their Horny Content
highlights.summary: A network of AI-generated models is using comics’ material to funnel views to their OnlyFans and Fanvue accounts—and there’s not much comedians can do about it.
body: Last week, the stand-up comedian Julia Jasunas was on Instagram when she got a DM from a fellow comic. Did she know, her friend wrote, that a random Instagram influencer had ripped off a joke from her stand-up act?

Initially, Jasunas was mad but not overly shocked. Plagiarism is not uncommon in the stand-up comedy world, and comics are “really sensitive about it, because there's not a ton of protection against it,” she tells WIRED. “So we all look out for each other.” Then she clicked on the link.

The video was of a purported stand-up comic named Aylen Skye, a buxom blond with leonine cheekbones and 250,000 Instagram followers. In the clip, Skye, wearing a crop top and Daisy Dukes, tells a joke about renting out a room in her two-bedroom apartment to a cute guy. To Jasunas’ shock, it was, verbatim, her joke, down to the “ums” and “ahs.”

highlights.title: 'Pokémon TCG Pocket' Announces Big Update to Address Player Concerns
highlights.summary: If you’ve played the mobile game Pokémon Trading Card Game Pocket, you probably have at least two major complaints: the UI is too slow, and the current card set release cadence is overwhelming. It seems that DeNa and The Pokémon Company are working on fixing at least one of these issues.
body: The Pokémon TCG Pocket Operations Team outlined additions and improvements coming to the game for its second anniversary. The biggest change is that new releases will come every six weeks instead of monthly.

While getting less content could be seen as a bad thing, TCG Pocket ​​​​'s rapid release schedule has overwhelmed many players. Whether you’re aiming to collect all the cards or trying to stay on top of the competitive meta, keeping up with the current release cycle requires near-religious devotion. The change to the game’s release calendar will start with the upcoming C series of card releases.

As for the deck-building experience, TCG Pocket is adding a Community Decks feature that lets you easily browse other players’ decks in-game and copy them. The developers are also attempting to improve the utility of rental decks and starter decks, giving them unlimited uses and making them available in versus play. Perhaps the most interesting addition to deck-building is Limited Battles, a new event type with a restricted card pool. These competitions will award players with accessories.

highlights.title: The last thing I did for my mother was illegal
highlights.summary: An urn cost more than my rent. So I scattered my mother’s ashes at Yosemite from a Ziploc bag, without the federal permit I couldn’t afford to wait for. My mother is in a Ziploc bag on my lap, wedged between a half-eaten bag of trail mix and my purse.
body: My stomach is queasy from the switchbacks up to Yosemite, where I’ve come to spread her ashes, and I’m having an existential crisis.
I had imagined this day as a beautiful send-off that would feel profound. Instead, it was all improvisation: a plastic bag, a last-minute decision, and ginger chews to stop me from being carsick.

I thought my 20s would be about kissing the wrong people in Los Angeles bars, not reading paperbacks on a hospital cot while my mom underwent her fifth brain surgery. My friends were off at college, debating sororities and semesters abroad; I was learning an entirely different set of skills.

At 21, I learned my mom had glioblastoma, a deadly brain cancer. Soon I was in the Bakersfield law library, Googling how to become my 16-year-old brother’s legal guardian, and learning that the same charm I used to snag me a table at Nobu could also get my mom a better room at Cedars-Sinai hospital. She ended up in the room Elizabeth Taylor had died in a few weeks earlier, a detail she loved to regale her friends with.

highlights.title: The Blood Of Dawnwalker’s Next Update Will Let You Erase Your Mistakes And Pet The Dog
highlights.summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker is already one of the best role-playing games of the year, but developer Rebel Wolves is preparing a big update that should make it even better. Like all good things in life, it starts with getting to pet a dog.
body: Update 1.1, which is scheduled to arrive next week, brings a number of new features to the game, including the ability to pet both dogs and cats via the game's directional system, which is currently only used for combat. It will also feature a new Story difficulty setting that provides "additional combat assist," new subtitle settings across all lines of dialogue, and most crucially, an item called Draught of Mind Rebirth.

The Draught of Mind Rebirth will allow you to forget all the skills and abilities you've acquired across the Swordmastery, Witchcraft, and Vampirism trees. Not only will this give you the chance to reallocate your points in a way that best fits your playstyle--it will also give you back the time associated with those skills. That means you'll have the chance to complete extra missions if you happen to find yourself impeded with Dawnwalker's 30-day limit. However, we don't find the system to be restrictive as it currently stands.

highlights.title: We’re Living in a Golden Age of Hot-Guy Politicians
highlights.summary: From Zohran Mamdani and Abdul El-Sayed to Jon Ossoff and Pete Buttigieg, a new generation of politicians is going hard on policy while being easy on the eyes.
body: According to political lore, the 1960 US election was, in part, determined by hotness. That year, John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon took part in the nation’s first televised presidential debates, giving a wide swath of the American public an alluring new metric by which to judge a could-be commander-in-chief. In one corner was the pale and clammy Nixon (who apparently refused hair and makeup on set), and in the other a freshly tanned, well-rested JFK. It’s said that those who listened on the radio assumed Nixon won, while those who caught the broadcast handily gave it to the camera-friendly Kennedy.

“Looks aren’t everything—they’re not the way we’re going to win,” says Lauren Kapp, a digital strategist who helped with Kamala Harris’s 2024 campaign. “People are focused on core issues; they’re looking for policy, and people who are talking about policy.” Still, “it’s a benefit if the person is more attractive,” she concedes. “Or if you see yourself in them.”

highlights.summary: Manchester United coach accepts defender’s apology. ‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough’ Michael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez not offering Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United’s director of football in the wake of Tuesday’s defeat…
body: Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.”

On Thursday Martínez issued an apology that did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said.

Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. “He’s released his statement, he’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough for all of us to move on with,” United’s manager said.

Carrick was pressed on whether it would have been better if Martínez had apologised to Wilcox and for his wider comments about investment, rather than just saying sorry for the timing and location of his interview. “From our point of view, the acknowledgment of what’s been done has certainly been enough, we’ve moved on and we’re definitely not looking back at it now,” he replied.

body: Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026. In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
The developer said it could not see “a clear path forward” for the game after several reworks, including its Heroes update. It said further changes would have made it almost a completely new game.

Squad Busters launched worldwide in May 2024. AppMagic estimates put its lifetime revenue at about $67.9m from 58.6m downloads, with the US accounting for 30% of spending. That works out at an estimated $1.16 in revenue per download globally.
The company has also ruled out offline play, private servers and releasing the code, saying the game contains content and characters from across its other titles.

highlights.title: Polymarket saw $600 million in election trades after the elections were over
highlights.summary: Prediction market boosters often tout the platforms as barometers of public opinion, or even “truth machines” offering a clearer picture of where things are headed than polling or other data. In 2024, for example, Kalshi beat many pollsters in forecasting the outcome of the US presidential race.
body: Two global election markets on Polymarket’s offshore platform, for instance, generated over $600 million in trading volume, far more than most political markets typically attract. Most of the activity took place buying and selling contracts tied to long-shot candidates who ultimately did not win.

Even odder? “Nearly all of it—about $284 million—came from pairs of accounts repeatedly buying and selling with each other,” says former Polymarket trader Chris Park, who now runs the prediction-market forensic analysis firm MSR Decode.

Such a high volume of seemingly pointless back-and-forth transactions has raised eyebrows among experts. “It’s obviously some form of volume manipulation,” says Rajiv Sethi, a Barnard College economics professor who researches prediction markets.

When asked about these markets, Shana Bautista, Polymarket’s head of global intelligence and investigations, told WIRED that the team “immediately flagged this activity, investigated, and blocked the accounts from trading.” Polymarket did not respond to follow-up questions about why the accounts were able to trade such a high amount of volume before it took action.

body: The Premier League champions are understood to have informed some, but not all, of the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season. Arsenal hope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.

It is understood the catering and travel departments are among the affected, and that the men’s and women’s first-team performance and coaching staff will not be impacted. The academy, Arsenal Women, Arsenal in the Community, the Arsenal Foundation and site security teams are also exempt, although other areas of the wider football operation are included in the review, which was overseen internally by the managing director, Richard Garlick.

The timing of the proposed cuts has attracted scrutiny after last week’s announcement of Arteta’s new contract, worth more than £20m a season. Arsenal say the restructuring process began before the deal was announced and the manager said he was not the appropriate person to answer questions about the redundancies.

highlights.summary: You can smell it in the air can't you? Feel the chill in your nostrils and the earthy scent as leaves fall and the sun departs for another year? body: I've been very excited about Bristol developer Friday Sundae's There are no Ghosts at the Grand ever since I saw it at a preview last year. It's one of those things that reads like a checklist of my very specific gaming interests, being part musical, part home renovation sim, and part ghostbusting mystery adventure, all unfolding in a dilapidated hotel in a British seaside town.

The idea is you've got 30 days to renovate it (exactly why is part of the mystery given its protagonist has motives so secret, he'll even try hiding them from the player), but there's plenty more to do besides: you can explore the cobblestone streets, go sailing out at sea, or take a scooter into the countryside as you attempt to uncover the truth about the hotel’s strange past. By night, there are ghosts to deal with - and throughout all this, the cast is prone to bursting into song. And if that tickles you fancy in the same way it's tickling mine, you can play a Steam demo right now ahead of its December arrival.

highlights.title: Veronica Roth Revives ‘Divergent’ in ‘The Sixth Faction’ (and Talks the Movie That Never Happened)
highlights.summary: The author talks carrying “anxiety baggage” about the book series, revisiting the story in an alternate-universe retelling and reflects on the film adaptations never getting an ending: "Everyone had moved forward."
body: Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

The Sixth Faction, released on Oct. 6, reimagines Roth’s bestselling series ( Divergent, Insurgent and Allegiant ), which is set in a post-apocalyptic society where citizens are divided into factions based on personality type. The first book in a planned duology is an alternate-universe retelling rather than a prequel or sequel, and it began as a personal project for Roth.

“ Divergent has this staying power that I wasn’t expecting,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter. “It’s hard for books to have that kind of lingering effect on a readership, and because it had that power, I thought I needed to course-correct my own feelings about it. I’d carried some anxiety baggage about Divergent, and I thought making something new would help me rediscover my love for the characters and the world. That’s where The Sixth Faction came from.”

highlights.title: On Location: Where was Tenzing filmed?
highlights.summary: We speak with director Jennifer Peedom and actors Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston about training in the Himalayan foothills and recreating Everest on New Zealand's Mount Cook.
body: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we ask: where was Tenzing filmed?

“Some of the most impactful people live in the dip of society,” says Tibetan actor Genden Phuntsok, who plays the film's namesake, Himalayan climber Tenzing Norgay. “There aren’t many stories about what Sherpas did before the mountaineers.” In Tenzing, Peedom looks at the first ascent of Everest through the lens of Tenzing, who summited alongside New Zealand mountaineer Sir Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) after persuading Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to give him a place on the British climbing team.

“Tenzing—as did Hillary— pushed the boundaries of what was imaginable,” says Hiddleston. “What the pair’s friendship can teach us is that there is strength in human fellowship. You begin as outsiders with different frames of reference, but we're more united by the things we share. Tenzing came from the higher Tibetan plateau, Hillary from New Zealand. They shared a love and respect for the mountains—and recognized each other.”
points: We speak with director Jennifer Peedom and actors Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston about training in the Himalayan foothills and recreating Everest on New Zealand's Mount Cook.
